topic: Thundering herd: coalescing requests for an uncached key so one fetch serves everyone (AWS Builders' Library)
text:
A cache doesn't only make things faster. It can also decide whether your database survives a bad minute.

The AWS Builders' Library calls one failure the "thundering herd": many clients request the same uncached resource at once. It can also happen when a server joins the fleet with an empty local cache.

The fix AWS describes: make sure only one pending request is out for an uncached resource. Everyone else waits for that result.

How I'd apply it:
1. Coalesce concurrent misses per key (many caching libraries and proxies like Nginx or Varnish support this).
2. Use a soft and a hard TTL, so stale data keeps serving while one request refreshes it.
3. Test your service with a cold cache, not just a warm one.

Takeaway: design for the cache being empty, because one day it will be.

Have you ever load-tested your system with a completely cold cache?
